nodes.question: What is highlighted as a limitation in the research findings?
nodes.answer: A limitation highlighted in the research findings is that a limited number of cases investigate slowing loops within the integration of digital technologies in Life Cycle Inventory development.
nodes.paragraph: Abstract Purpose This research aims to develop a critical understanding of the employment of digital technologies (DTs) for LCA studies, outlining both the opportunities and challenges associated with circular strategies. Two research questions are thus addressed: (1) What circular loops and aspects are addressed when digital technologies are integrated in the development of a Life Cycle Inventory? (2) Which trade-offs are revealed in the integration of digital technologies in Life Cycle Inventory development addressing circularity along a life cycle? Methods This study is based on the problematisation approach, which critically examines existing assumptions in the LCA literature, structured into six principles: defining a domain of investigation, articulating and evaluating assumptions, develop- ing alternative perspectives, involving the audience through qualitative interviews, and assessing the alternative assumptions. A systematic literature review (SLR) and semi-structured interviews with experts were conducted to explore these issues and suggest future research directions. Results and discussion It emerges that the DTs are mainly integrated in the Life Cycle Inventory phase capturing closing and narrowing loops, whereas a limited number of cases investigate slowing loops with different aspects investigated.

nodes.question: What research questions guided this study?
nodes.answer: The research questions that guided the study are: 1) What circular loops are addressed when digital technologies are integrated into the development of a Life Cycle Inventory? 2) What trade-offs are revealed in the integration of digital technologies in Life Cycle Inventory development addressing circularity along a life cycle?
nodes.paragraph: 2020; Sica et al. 2022) Moving from this background, this research aims to develop a deeper and more critical understanding of the integration of DTs into LCA, outlining both the opportuni- ties and challenges associated with circular strategies. To this end, this research questions existing assumptions and develops new research perspectives. Emerging positions from the literature regarding the role of DTs for LCA studies are discussed, with a specific focus on the Life Cycle Inven- tory (LCI). Specifically, the research questions that guided the study are the following: RQ1: What circular loops are addressed when digital technologies are integrated into the development of a Life Cycle Inventory? RQ2: What trade-offs are revealed in the integration of digital technologies in Life Cycle Inventory development addressing circularity along a life cycle? The findings of this study are expected to contribute to the existing body of knowledge on LCA by providing detailed insights into how DTs can enhance the development of LCI, promoting the business circular transition. Additionally, the study offers practical recommendations for organisations seeking to implement these technologies to achieve more sustainable and efficient production systems.

nodes.question: What is the focus of dos Santos et al.'s work on distributed economies in the context of sustainability?
nodes.answer: The focus of dos Santos et al.'s work on distributed economies is on designing sustainability for all, as detailed in their publication in Lecture Notes in Mechanical Engineering.
